# Recording a click without slowing the redirect

> `recordClick` sends a `link.clicked` event to Kafka without waiting for it and ignores any failure, so the redirect never waits on Kafka, and the controller skips it when the edge already counted the click.

_Part of [Link click attribution and stats](link-click-analytics.md)_

A visit to `GET /l/:code` lands in the `redirect` method of the controller. It first looks up the link with `resolve` and returns 404 if there is none. Then it decides whether to record the click. The edge worker can serve cached redirects itself and tells the origin it already counted the click by sending the header `x-edge-click-recorded: 1`. If that header is anything else, the controller calls `recordClick` with the country (from `cf-ipcountry`) and the referer. `recordClick` is a plain method, not an async one. It builds a [`link.clicked` event](link-clicked-event.md) with a fresh time-ordered [`uuidv7`](../../../../packages/backend/scripts/load-tests/lib/utils.js#L14) click id, the code, the current time, the country, the referer cut to 300 characters, and the via-edge flag. It hands the event to the Kafka producer, with the code as the message key. It does not await the send. A trailing `.catch(() => undefined)` swallows errors, so a Kafka outage can't fail or slow the redirect. The controller then sets the `ref` query parameter to the code, adds `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=10`, and answers with a 302. The event is stored later by the projector, described in [Link click attribution and stats](link-click-analytics.md).

**Look at:** [share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts) · [share-links.controller.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/api/share-links.controller.ts)

## Pieces

- [Kafka send that is not awaited and ignores errors](fire-and-forget-send.md): `recordClick` returns nothing and starts the producer send with `void` and a `.catch` that does nothing, so the response never waits for Kafka.
- [Skip when the edge already counted the click](edge-already-recorded-check.md): The controller only calls `recordClick` when the `x-edge-click-recorded` header is not `1`, so a click is not counted twice.
- [The link.clicked event and its payload](link-clicked-event.md): The versioned event that carries click id, code, time, country, referer and via-edge flag.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| queue | ```link.clicked`` event on the `links` topic (``LinkClicked.topic``)` | Written by `recordClick` with the link code as the message key, so clicks on one link stay in order. |
| api | ``GET /l/:code`` | Reads the headers `cf-ipcountry`, `referer` and `x-edge-click-recorded`, then answers with a 302 redirect. |

## Watch out

- A failed Kafka send is lost without a log or a retry, so click counts can be a little low during an outage.
- The skip depends only on the `x-edge-click-recorded` header being exactly `1`. Any other value, or no header, records the click at the origin.
- The `viaEdge` field defaults to `false`, and the controller does not pass it, so clicks recorded at the origin always have `viaEdge` false.
- The `LinkClicked.create` call is given the code as its second argument along with a `0`, and the click itself is keyed by the code, so a very popular link sends all its clicks to one partition.
